data.hypothesis: The catalog has one distinct valid T2 program and no repeated program; its two-pass AVX-512 implementation measured 0.526 microseconds versus the baseline's 4.463 microseconds. This candidate preserves that algorithm but uses four independent signed-minimum accumulators in the first pass to test whether the parent's loop-carried vector-minimum dependency limits throughput. The extra accumulator state and final merge may offset the benefit, so performance remains uncertain.

memory_lessons.applicability: Keep the measured two-pass implementation as the comparison point; the unrolled first pass has not yet been measured.
memory_lessons.claim: The existing two-pass parent was valid and correct across five checked cases, with mean time 5.2559e-7 seconds; the baseline mean was 4.4632e-6 seconds. These measurements do not establish the effect of independent accumulators.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Run correctness first, then compare repeated timings on the frozen protocol, including random and decreasing inputs.

data.notes: This changes only src/candidate.cpp and retains the parent’s signed two-pass search and first-index tie handling. The parent’s reported correctness and timings are measured facts; this candidate has not been built, correctness-checked, or timed here. Have the controller check correctness before repeated timing, including random and decreasing cases, ties, INT32 extrema, scalar tails, and valid sizes. Keep the compiler, target, and protocol frozen.
transformations: Replace the first-pass single vector-minimum recurrence with four independent AVX-512 signed-minimum accumulators over groups of four vectors, then merge their minima.
Process remaining complete vectors and the scalar tail as before; retain the second-pass vector equality scan and lowest matching lane to preserve earliest-index ties.
